pages.headline: Two labs claim the death of the Exponential Time Hypothesis
pages.deck: OpenAI, then Anthropic hours later, say their models produced sub-exponential algorithms for a hard class of logic problems. Outside reviewers are now checking the proofs.

sentences: Anthropic filed to go public, disclosing $131.7 billion in cash and investments, and chip stocks rallied for a third consecutive session on the news.

OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-tier computer-use model priced at half its predecessor, and said its models produced three mathematical results including a claimed refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
Within hours, Anthropic claimed a refutation of its own, leaving outside shepherds to decide whether either proof survives review.
Google DeepMind previewed Genie 4, a world model that generates interactive scenes with sound, while Meta open-sourced the 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open for agentic coding.
The money kept moving: Tenstorrent raised a $1.5 billion Series E at a $6.2 billion valuation, and Guidewire agreed to acquire hyperexponential for $1.7 billion in cash.
Underneath the rally, investors kept debating whether debt-funded AI capital expenditure can pay for itself.

items.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra
items.one_liner: OpenAI's mid-tier computer-use model lands at $1 per million input tokens — half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and more than three times faster.
items.take: The price cut, not the benchmark, is the story.

items.headline: Genie 4
items.one_liner: Google DeepMind's world model generates interactive scenes with native audio and real-time steering, in research preview for trusted testers.

sources.excerpt: DeepMind announced Genie 4, a multimodal world model that natively generates audio, ambient sound, and interactive dialogue, can be steered in real time via natural language, and is being rolled out as a research preview to trusted testers.

items.headline: Muse Spark Open
items.one_liner: Meta's 816-billion-parameter open-weight MoE targets long-running coding agents, with 42 billion parameters active per token and a one-million-token context.

sources.excerpt: Meta has published Muse Spark Open, an open-weight multimodal model designed for long-running coding agents. The mixture-of-experts system combines text, images, audio, and video with approximately 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active for each token.

items.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra on Terminal-Bench 4.0

sources.excerpt: OpenAI reports that it scores 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at max effort, against a published 21.5% for its predecessor. All of OpenAI's figures are company-reported, and no independent evaluation had been published by the end of Monday.

items.headline: A statement, not a question
items.one_liner: OpenAI says its models found sub-exponential algorithms for a hard class of logic puzzles; Anthropic reportedly claimed its own refutation hours later. Outside shepherds are organising expert groups to verify each result.

sources.excerpt: OpenAI announced on 26 October that its models found sub-exponential algorithms for a hard class of logic puzzles, which would make the Exponential Time Hypothesis false, and The Information reports that Anthropic claimed its own refutation hours later.
OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics. The Verge covered the announcement of three results in maths, computer science and physics.

items.headline: Can debt-funded AI capital expenditure pay for itself?
items.one_liner: Relief rally or reckoning: Anthropic's IPO paperwork lifted chip stocks all week, while investors keep asking whether borrowing-fuelled data-centre spend earns its cost of capital.

sources.excerpt: An AI-fueled tech rally sent US stocks to a higher close on Tuesday. The buzz surrounding details of Anthropic's impending initial public offering helped boost chip stocks for the third consecutive session. Growing concerns over the viability of debt-funded spending have weighed on the AI trade.

Stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry led Wall Street higher on Tuesday. AI stocks rose to another winning day after swerving for weeks on worries about whether their boom is under threat because of how expensive they have become.
